thread:
Michael S.: Heads up — Keystone sent back their RFI + a security spreadsheet. They're asking for a capability matrix, POC runbook, and clarification on burst pricing for Dedicated. Can we triage?
Anya G.: Adding the checklist I used for Nova — will attach baseline matrix (keystone_rfi_matrix_draft.csv).
Samir R.: POC asks look heavy: 2-week Dedicated with 8xA100 equiv, KV cache preserved between sessions, data retention 30 days, and ability to swap quantized model if perf regresses. Is that doable?
Elaine (Security): On the SQ we need confirm on KMS integration + SOC2/ISO artifacts. I can provide the standard pack but need confirmation on whether they require HSM-backed keys for Private.
Jules - Sales Ops: Pricing question: they want burst capacity for spikes — request says "up to 3x baseline for 1–2 hours/day". Do we price as overage or a short-term reserve?
Michael S.: Primary ask from Keystone: predictable latency under load. They called out "99th p50 target < 120ms for chat flows" and want an A/B that falls back to a cheaper model if latency > 200ms.
Samir R.: For latency SLOs we can recommend Dedicated + autoscale with a burst pool. Implementation detail: enable slow-start to avoid cold-start thrash. Suggest config snippet to include in the runbook:
```
service: dedicated-inference
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 4
  burst_pool: 8
  scale_interval_s: 30
fallback:
  policy: route-to-quantized
```
Anya G.: I'll fold that into the POC runbook. Also flagging that the customer requires evaluation of embeddings accuracy after quantization — need a short eval harness and baseline prompts.
Elaine (Security): Attachments I'll include: SOC2 attestation, pen-test summary, KMS integration notes. If they require HSM, that's a legal + deployment change for Private; we should outline tradeoffs.
Jules - Sales Ops: For burst pricing: propose a two-part quote — reserved baseline + burst credit blocks (billed per-block used). Example line item: "Reserved 8 GPUs + 24 burst-credit-hours per month, excess at 1.8x unit rate." Thoughts?
Michael S.: Sounds reasonable. Can we get engineering to sign off on the 1.8x multiplier? Also need an explicit rollback plan if quantized model decreases quality by >3% on their eval set.
Samir R.: Signoff: 1.8x is feasible as an ops proxy. For rollback — include automatic canary and immediate route-back to float model, plus a manual escalation step to ops. I'll draft the revert steps.
Anya G.: I'll produce: keystone_rfi_matrix_v1.csv, keystone_poc_runbook_v1.md, keystone_eval_harness.zip (list of prompts + metrics). ETA EOD tomorrow for drafts.
Elaine (Security): I'll attach security artifacts and add a short note about HSM path + lead time. Expect docs by tomorrow afternoon.
infra-bot: Reminder: upload links to artifacts instead of attachments in Slack — large files fail. Use secure file share link.
Jules - Sales Ops: I'll draft the pricing appendix with both reserved + burst options and a sample contract clause for data residency. Will ping legal for HSM pricing uplift.
Michael S.: Great — plan: Anya compiles matrix + runbook, Samir finalizes ops config + rollback steps, Elaine provides security pack, Jules assembles pricing appendix. We'll do a 30-min sync tomorrow 10:30 PT to review before sending.
Samir R.: One more ask — can we include a brief perf table showing expected p50/p99 per model variant and token length? I can generate with the benchmarking scripts.
Anya G.: Yup, I'll add perf table to the matrix CSV.
Michael S.: Thanks team. I'll consolidate everything into the RFI response bundle and send to Keystone after the 10:30 sync. :thumbsup:
